clue.text: Novel tall story

blocks.note: first meaning: Arnold Bennett's 1908 novel about two sisters in the Potteries
second meaning: a piece of folklore or superstition passed on without evidence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective describing the story, but it is a definition in its own right: the title of a book by Arnold Bennett.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names Bennett's novel and is also the idiom for an unfounded traditional belief, which is a kind of tall story.

clue.text: Offer too much for love -- a word that is the same in Latin

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O
a verb is a part of speech, and verbum is Latin for a word
id. abbreviates the Latin idem, meaning the same

explanation.surface: A lover pays over the odds, and the setter muses on a word that is identical in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: ID is the scholarly abbreviation of idem, used in footnotes to mean the same source again.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbid is to make a bid higher than the thing is worth, at auction or in cards.

clue.text: Resident has 500 boots

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
Sam Weller is the boots, the shoe-cleaning servant, at the White Hart inn in Dickens's Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: Someone living here owns five hundred pairs of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boots' looks like footwear but is a job title: an inn's boots cleaned guests' shoes, and Dickens's most famous boots is Sam Weller.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is someone who lives in a place, so a resident of it.

clue.text: Bar could be in credit by end of account

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word that follows
could be suggests the letters might turn into something else if rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of account

explanation.surface: A banking picture: the balance is positive by the time the statement closes.
explanation.definitionFit: To interdict is to forbid or prohibit, which is one sense of to bar someone from something.

clue.text: Rules of conduct of the race not new

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular noun: an ethic is a set of such rules

indicators.note: not tells us a letter standing for the following word must be removed

blocks.note: ethnic means relating to a race or people
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A code of behaviour belonging to a people, nothing modern about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle or body of principles governing how a person behaves.

clue.text: Stalky &Co., for example, awarded eight lines

blocks.note: Kipling's Stalky & Co. is about three schoolboy friends, so they make a trio
let means allowed or granted

explanation.surface: Kipling's schoolboys are given eight lines as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Stalky & Co. is Kipling's 1899 book about Stalky, Beetle and M'Turk at boarding school. The eight lines look like a school imposition but are a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A triolet is a short French verse form of exactly eight lines with only two rhymes and repeated lines.

clue.text: Told an untruth? Then admit the rest

definitions.note: noun phrase for a verb phrase: to lie down is to take a rest

blocks.note: lied is the past tense meaning told an untruth
to own (up to) something is to admit it

explanation.surface: Someone tells a fib and is then urged to confess everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest' reads as the remainder of the confession, but it means a period of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a lie-down is having a short rest, typically on a bed or sofa.

clue.text: Parry on demo has to retrace his steps

blocks.note: to counter a blow is to parry it
a demonstration is often a protest march

explanation.surface: A fencer's parry during a protest forces him to back off.
explanation.definitionFit: A countermarch is a military manoeuvre in which a column turns and marches back the way it came.

clue.text: Everyone is wearing plain stuff

indicators.note: something being worn sits inside its clothing, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: overt means plain to see, open
ea. abbreviates each, which here stands for everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody is dressed in simple material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun meaning fabric, which suits the clothing picture, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to eat far too much, which is exactly what overeating means.

clue.text: She is an Official Receiver

blocks.note: surface reading: a woman holds the government post that winds up bankrupt estates
setter's reading: a woman who is legally entitled to receive an estate when someone dies

explanation.walkthrough: The Official Receiver is a real British post administering bankruptcies; here it simply means a woman officially in line to receive property.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who will legally inherit property is the person officially designated to receive it.

clue.text: Dickensian who did his best at the end

definitions.text: Dickensian who did his best at the end

blocks.clueFragment: Dickensian who did his best at the end
blocks.note: surface reading: some Dickens character who tried hard as things finished

blocks.clueFragment: did his best at the end
blocks.note: setter's reading: the hero of A Tale of Two Cities who goes to the guillotine saying it is a far, far better thing that he does than he has ever done

explanation.walkthrough: The clue alludes to the closing line of A Tale of Two Cities, where the dissolute lawyer redeems himself by dying in another man's place.
explanation.definitionFit: The character's famous last words claim his sacrifice is the best deed of his life, done at its very end.

clue.text: Swindler's impressive capture of bishop with rook

indicators.note: a capture holds its prize inside, so the next piece is taken into the word before

blocks.note: noble means grand or impressive
B is the chess notation for bishop
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess move: a fine capture of a bishop using the rook.
explanation.walkthrough: To nobble is British slang for to cheat, or to tamper with a racehorse or bribe a juror.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobbler is one who nobbles, that is cheats or tampers dishonestly, so a swindler.

clue.text: Cold oil can become gluey

indicators.note: can become says these letters are able to turn into a new word when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Chilled oil thickens into something sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means glue-like or gelatinous; its root is the Greek kolla, glue.

clue.text: By the sound of it, a mountain duck

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to judge by hearing, so we want a word pronounced like the next one

blocks.note: Mount Ida is a mountain in Crete, and another near Troy

explanation.surface: A duck that, from its call, seems to live on a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck whose soft down is used to fill quilts.

clue.text: I'm going to change about 39 books -- it's a weakness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the next

blocks.note: taken as written
pence are small coins, loose change
the Old Testament has 39 books in the Protestant canon

explanation.surface: Someone plans to swap roughly 39 volumes, then confesses a failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb but means coins, and 'about' looks like approximately but is the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotence is powerlessness or lack of strength, so a weakness.

clue.text: Long to have one or another fruit

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
another fruit: the apple, with the closing word doing double duty

explanation.surface: Someone craves a single piece of fruit, or else a different kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical plant whose large juicy fruit has a spiky skin and leafy crown.

clue.text: The cocktail island

blocks.note: first meaning: a drink of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters
second meaning: the island at the heart of New York City

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a bar on an island; the two words name the same thing in different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is named after the New York borough, which occupies an island between the Hudson and East rivers.

clue.text: A born idiot - that's a certainty

blocks.note: first meaning: an old term for a person simple-minded from birth
second meaning: something sure to succeed

explanation.surface: Someone is declared a fool from birth, beyond any doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaically a natural was a person of low intelligence from birth; colloquially a natural is a sure thing or born winner.

clue.text: A very full volume torn to pieces - what an insult!

definitions.note: the exclamation stands for the noun insult

indicators.note: something in pieces has been broken up, so its letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge tome has been ripped apart, and the owner is outraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like a book, which suits the tearing, but here it means loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is a deliberate insult or slight to someone's dignity.

clue.text: Continent as detailed in poetry

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, it says the word loses its tail, its last letter

blocks.note: a continent

explanation.surface: A continent as it is described in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as described minutely, but split it as de-tailed. Poets such as Milton shorten the name to fit the metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Afric is the archaic poetic form of the continent's name, found in older English verse.

clue.text: The sort of place where holidaymakers board

definitions.text: The sort of place where holidaymakers board

blocks.clueFragment: The sort of place where holidaymakers board
blocks.note: surface reading: a guest house or resort where tourists take board and lodging
setter's reading: board means get on, as passengers do a plane

explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests board and lodging at a seaside boarding house; it means climbing aboard a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers leaving on holiday get on their planes at this kind of terminal.

clue.text: The wine served up in Jordan is terrible

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down clue served up means brought upwards, so the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: The wine offered in Jordan is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Volunteers in the Air Force get one a drink

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the Royal Air Force
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reservists serving with the RAF buy someone a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is a sweet liqueur flavoured with almonds or fruit kernels.

clue.text: Country where the bread rises miraculously

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the bread that fell from heaven for the Israelites
surface padding that hints at the heavenly bread of Exodus

explanation.surface: A land where loaves rise as if by a miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rises' suggests dough rising in the oven; it is the upward reading. 'Miraculously' only points to the heavenly bread of Exodus.
explanation.definitionFit: Annam was a historic kingdom and later French protectorate forming central Vietnam.

clue.text: Having no Home Guard., Harrogate improvised this gas-charger

indicators.note: having no says some letters are taken away
something improvised is made up on the spot, so the letters are thrown together afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
HG abbreviates the Home Guard, Britain's wartime volunteer force

explanation.surface: Without its wartime defenders, the Yorkshire spa town knocked up a gadget for fizzy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerator charges a liquid with air or gas, as in making carbonated water.

clue.text: Maritime missile is nothing to rabbit on about

blocks.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter on, and to harp is to go on about something
nothing is zero, which looks like O
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sea-going weapon is said to be no big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for to talk at tiresome length.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired at whales and large fish at sea.

clue.text: Condition a terrorist is in

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a Provo was a member of the Provisional IRA
taken as written

explanation.surface: A report on the state of a captured gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is in' reads as part of the sentence; 'is' is the inserted piece and 'in' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or clause attached to an agreement, a condition that must be met.

clue.text: Ancient lady killer can set Myrtle in a whirl

indicators.note: whirling spins things round, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A murderess could send poor Myrtle spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady killer' suggests a womaniser, but it means a woman who kills.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this queen of Mycenae murdered her husband Agamemnon on his return from Troy.
